html:
A Kurdish soldier who became sultan of Egypt and Syria and founded the Ayyubid dynasty of Ayyubid and Mamluk Egypt. He took Jerusalem from the crusaders in 1187.

Born in Tikrit, he served Nur al-Din, the Turkish ruler of Syria, and went with his uncle to Fatimid Egypt, where he became vizier in 1169. Two years later he ended the Fatimid caliphate and returned Egypt to Sunni Islam. After Nur al-Din died he took Damascus and Aleppo, joining Egypt and Syria for the first time in centuries.

In July 1187 he destroyed the crusader army at the Battle of Hattin, and in October he took Jerusalem, letting most of its people buy their freedom. This set off the Third Crusade. Richard the Lionheart retook Acre and beat him at Arsuf but never reached Jerusalem, and in 1192 they agreed a truce that let Christian pilgrims visit. Saladin died in Damascus in 1193 and is buried beside the Umayyad Mosque. European writers admired him as a model of chivalry.
sum: A Kurdish soldier who became sultan of Egypt and Syria and founded the Ayyubid dynasty of Ayyubid and Mamluk Egypt. He took Jerusalem from the crusaders in 1187.
